Dear Rajni,

I'm writing this instead of saying it, because I'm a coward about saying it.

Last Friday, when the anonymous school confessions page posted the clip of you singing at the assembly, the comments were already crazy. Hundreds. Everyone was adding something. I scrolled for ten minutes and then I added one too, under a made-up name. It was mean. I won't repeat it.

I keep trying to explain how it felt. It didn't feel like me typing. You felt far away, like a picture, and everyone else was doing it, so it seemed like just one more drop in the rain. But it was my thumb. On Monday I saw you eat lunch alone in the library, and I knew which drop was mine.

I've deleted it. I'm sorry. Your high note was actually good.

Jasleen (the girl two rows behind you in maths)

qa.a: Jasleen saw Rajni eat lunch alone in the library.

qa.a: Rajni felt far away like a picture, the name was made up and everyone else was commenting, so it felt like one more drop in the rain.

qa.a: She deleted the comment and wrote to apologise; she could also report the clip to a teacher so the page takes it down.

qa.q: How might Rajni feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Rajni may feel a mix of hurt and relief, hurt to know a classmate joined in, but glad someone admitted it and praised Rajni's high note.
